headline: DJI Osmo Pocket 4P adds a 3x telephoto lens, hailed as a top gimbal camera
summary: The new DJI Osmo Pocket 4P features an impressive 3x telephoto lens, enhancing its video capabilities. However, due to ongoing issues, it won't be released in the US market.
details: The DJI Osmo Pocket 4P introduces a second 3x telephoto lens, building on the Osmo Pocket 4. It's priced at £529 / €599 (about $680) for the Standard Combo in Europe, offering a strong competitor to Insta360's Luna Ultra.

Despite its launch elsewhere, the Pocket 4P will not be released in the US due to DJI's ongoing regulatory challenges. Hopes for a US version via 'front companies' like Xtra have diminished, with preorders halted and refunds issued.

The 4P shares the exact same body, controls, and flip-out touchscreen as the original Pocket 4. Its main camera is nearly identical, with software, stabilization, recording options, and in-built storage remaining consistent.

The new 3x telephoto (60mm equivalent) lens sits above the default camera. It features a 1/1.28-inch-type sensor and a fast f/1.8 aperture, supporting 4K landscape or 3K portrait video and 37-megapixel stills in various modes.

The telephoto lens delivers impressive quality with crisp details, benefiting from the same excellent gimbal stabilization. Footage remains remarkably steady, even in challenging conditions like a blustery boat trip.

The Pocket 4P can record 4K footage up to 12x zoom, though quality degrades beyond 6x. Its wide f/1.8 aperture creates beautiful optical bokeh, making it ideal for product, portrait, or pet videography.

Despite its launch elsewhere, the Pocket 4P will not be released in the US due to DJI's ongoing regulatory challenges. Hopes for a US version via 'front companies' like Xtra have diminished, with preorders halted and refunds issued.

The 4P shares the exact same body, controls, and flip-out touchscreen as the original Pocket 4. Its main camera is nearly identical, with software, stabilization, recording options, and in-built storage remaining consistent.

The new 3x telephoto (60mm equivalent) lens sits above the default camera. It features a 1/1.28-inch-type sensor and a fast f/1.8 aperture, supporting 4K landscape or 3K portrait video and 37-megapixel stills in various modes.

headline: Jony Ive's OpenAI hardware device sounds like a HomePod
summary: Reports suggest Jony Ive and Sam Altman's teased AI hardware device will resemble Apple's HomePod, combining smart display and speaker functionalities.
details: Jony Ive and Sam Altman have been teasing an AI hardware device for some time. Recent reports indicate this device will likely combine smart display features with a speaker, reminiscent of Apple's HomePod.

The collaboration between the former Apple design chief and the OpenAI CEO aims to create a new category of AI-powered consumer electronics. This venture seeks to integrate advanced AI capabilities into a user-friendly physical form factor.

While specific features remain unconfirmed, the device is expected to offer intuitive voice interaction and potentially visual AI responses. Its design is anticipated to prioritize simplicity and seamless integration into daily life, a hallmark of Ive's previous work.

The project is backed by significant funding, highlighting the ambition to redefine how users interact with artificial intelligence. Further details on its capabilities and release timeline are expected as development progresses.
